title: Create, Update, and Delete Operations
description: Perform robust mutations using create, createMany, update, upsert, and delete with transaction safety and relational nesting.

data.text: Mutating data in Prisma is handled through explicit mutation methods. Beyond basic single-record insertions and deletions, Prisma supports **nested writes** (creating parent and child records in a single atomic database transaction) and **upserts** (updating a record if it exists, or inserting it if it does not).

One of Prisma's most powerful capabilities is nested writes. You can create a parent record and multiple related child records in a single query invocation. Prisma automatically executes them within an internal transaction, ensuring complete atomicity.

data.title: Nested Create: User with Initial Profile and Posts
data.content: Creates the User, UserProfile, and multiple Posts atomically.

data.text: `upsert` is essential for idempotency, background webhooks (e.g. Stripe checkout events), and OAuth profile synchronization. In PostgreSQL, Prisma compiles `upsert` directly into an `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (...) DO UPDATE` statement.

data.title: OAuth Profile Sync with Upsert
data.content: If the user exists, update their profile picture and last login; if not, create them.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Nested writes wrap insertions across multiple tables in a single database transaction.
`upsert` uses native PostgreSQL `ON CONFLICT` for race-condition-free synchronization.
`createMany` is drastically faster than running `create` in a `for` loop.
